summary: The affine-hit closure follows from exact load truncation, the accepted planar lattice-center assertion, and the common affine witness, which gives the required Chebyshev-radius bound. The weighted distance problem is correctly recast as distance from a compact convex product to the affine-evaluation subspace; its stated dual, attainment, complementarity, support contacts, load bound, and force and moment equations are valid. Scaling each actual selected edge by its target load ratio produces a legal nonzero subfamily with support exactly J_x, so the accepted rank-at-most-one closure correctly forces full planar affine rank. All constants, strict inequalities, quantifiers, and boundary cases check out.
